signals.title: NZD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Hawkish BoJ Divergence
signals.text: JPY outperformance (+2.298%, n=7) vs NZD weakness (-1.445%, n=4) creates a 3.742% G10 spread, setting up downside pressure on NZD/JPY into the Sydney/Tokyo open. BoJ rate hike speculation and hawkish policymaker rhetoric run counter to the 175bp nominal carry deficit, accelerating cross unwinds as JPY momentum dominates. The BoJ meeting on 18 Sep determines whether policy normalization validates the JPY rally. Trade bias: Bearish NZD/JPY into the weekly open. Catalyst: Sydney/Tokyo open followed by the BoJ meeting on 18 Sep. Risk: A rebound above key technical resistance or aggressive carry restoration invalidates downside momentum.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Leveraged Short Squeeze + Hawkish BoJ Headlines
signals.text: JPY COT LF short -111.3k (pctl 2, z -2.18) establishes severe short-squeeze risk — USD/JPY closed Friday at 156.22 after breaking below its SMA20 (158.96) and SMA200 (158.45). Mounting calls from BoJ hawks for rate hikes alongside strong options put skew (25d RR -2.54) drive accelerated liquidation of crowded dollar-yen longs despite the +268bp SOFR-TONA carry buffer. The BoJ meeting on 18 Sep resolves whether further policy tightening forces an extended positioning wash-out. Trade bias: Short USD/JPY targeting deeper retracement below 156.00. Catalyst: Tokyo open followed by the Fed meeting on 16 Sep and BoJ meeting on 18 Sep. Risk: Daily close back above the 200-day SMA at 158.45 aborts the short-squeeze dynamic.
evidence: USD/JPY closed Friday at 156.22 (below SMA20 158.96 and SMA200 158.45)

signals.title: EUR/USD — Crowded Leveraged Short vs ECB Hike Bias
signals.text: EUR COT LF short -52.8k (pctl 4, z -2.15) creates stretched downside positioning risk — EUR/USD closed Friday at 1.1621 right near its SMA20 (1.1611). Persistent ESTR-SOFR carry drag (-147bp) maintains baseline resistance, but the ECB's explicit hike bias ahead of this week's decision leaves shorts vulnerable to a squeeze. The ECB meeting on 10 Sep determines whether monetary policy divergence forces an unwind of leveraged short exposure. Trade bias: Bullish EUR/USD on positioning mean-reversion toward 1.1700. Catalyst: ECB meeting on 10 Sep. Risk: ECB holds rates and shifts to a dovish guidance stance, invalidating the squeeze setup.
evidence: EUR/USD closed Friday at 1.1621 vs SMA20 1.1611
ECB next meeting on 10 Sep (bias: Hike)

signals.title: AUD/USD — Crowded Long Positioning vs Retail Short Divergence
signals.text: AUD COT LF long +50.3k (pctl 94, z +1.79) creates crowded-long unwind risk — AUD/USD closed Friday at 0.7205 above all major moving averages. Institutional positioning extremes diverge sharply from retail sentiment (90% short), while positive AONIA-SOFR carry (+69bp) and resilient commodity prices buffer against immediate liquidation. The RBA meeting on 29 Sep determines whether neutral policy settings can sustain current speculative length. Trade bias: Neutral-to-bearish AUD/USD on stretched leveraged length into the open. Catalyst: Sydney open and RBA meeting on 29 Sep. Risk: Break below SMA20 at 0.7135 triggers a broader institutional liquidation wave.
evidence: AUD/USD closed Friday at 0.7205 vs SMA20 0.7135

signals.title: USD/CAD — Crowded Leveraged Short Ahead of BoC Decision
signals.text: CAD COT LF short -70.1k (pctl 10, z -1.44) sets up short-covering squeeze potential — USD/CAD closed Friday at 1.3837, testing its SMA200 (1.3833). Although USD holds a +136bp SOFR-CORRA carry advantage, elevated WTI crude prices at $91.50 reinforce CAD terms-of-trade support and cap topside momentum. The BoC meeting on 9 Sep resolves whether domestic policy guidance accelerates covering of speculative Canadian Dollar shorts. Trade bias: Bearish USD/CAD on failure to hold above the 200-day SMA. Catalyst: BoC meeting on 9 Sep. Risk: Firm break above SMA20 at 1.3861 invalidates downside momentum and targets 1.4000.
evidence: USD/CAD closed Friday at 1.3837 vs SMA200 1.3833
BoC next meeting on 9 Sep (bias: Hold)
